title: MODIFY … UPDATE FIELDS ( … ) blanks a field that already had a value
symptom: After a write-back (e.g. results of an external API call), rows that already had a result lose it: the field is initial in the database.
rootCause: UPDATE FIELDS ( f1 f2 ) builds the control flags from the field list for every row alike, so a row with an initial f1 overwrites the stored value with blank.

solutions.label: Drop those rows from the write pipeline
solutions.body: Filter right after READ ENTITIES (e.g. DELETE lt_row WHERE Result IS NOT INITIAL) so the rows that must keep their value never reach the MODIFY.

solutions.label: Two MODIFY statements
solutions.body: One per field group; the second fed only with the rows that should get the value. (Per-row %control with UPDATE SET FIELDS WITH: not verified.)

prevention: Unit-test write-backs with a mix of filled and initial values.
